newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal, facing soaring escudo, cuts repo rate.
newsitem.headline: Portugal, facing soaring escudo, cuts repo rate.

text.p: The Bank of Portugal, facing a soaring escudo, cut its repurchase pact rate by 20 basis points to 6.50 percent on Friday, taking some analysts by surprise.
The central bank left its absorption rate used to drain funds from the money market unchanged at 6.20 percent and its emergency lending rate steady at 8.30 percent.

Isabel Cabral an analyst with Lisbon broker Fincor said: "It is a little surprising and is a consequence of the rise of the escudo against the mark. There is room for a further cut in the repo rate, and possibly also the absorption rate, by the end of February."
Mario Dias Vigario of Morgan Grenfell said: "I think that this decision by the Bank of Portugal is well-considered and is a result of the recent appreciation of the escudo against the mark."
He added: "It is preferable to cut the repo rate than to intervene in the foreign exchange market to limit the rise of the escudo," he added.
The Bank of Portugal bought marks at 99.68 escudos early on Friday to avoid the rapid appreciation of the escudo, dealers said. The Bank of Portugal declined comment.
Foreign investors, confident in the performance of the Portuguese economy, bought the escudo heavily throughout the week, dealers said.
One trader said: "The problem facing the Bank of Portugal is not the sentiment, but the speed with which the escudo is rising, and so the central bank started buying marks."
The escudo stood at 99.70/74 per mark in afternoon trade.
